heroHeadline: PLA STC Launches Combat Readiness Patrols at Scarborough Following USCG Midgett Exercise; China CCG Deploys East of Taiwan After Japan-Philippines Maritime Boundary Talks; Xiang Yang Hong 33 Day 26
heroSubtitle: China's PLA Southern Theater Command executed 'combat readiness patrols' in the territorial waters and airspace of Scarborough Shoal on June 1, 2026 — a direct military counter-signal one day after the USCG Midgett (WMSL-757) and PCG BRP Melchora Aquino completed their five-day joint presence operations at the disputed feature (May 28–31, the third US-Philippine coast guard bilateral presence at Scarborough in 2026). Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro, speaking from the Shangri-La Dialogue, declared Manila remains under 'severe threat' from China: 'We have no choice but really to be resilient and to stand up against Chinese aggression.' Simultaneously, China's Coast Guard deployed patrols in waters east of Taiwan on June 1 as a coercive response to Japan and the Philippines formally launching maritime boundary delimitation talks following the Takaichi-Marcos summit in Tokyo on May 29 — China declared the talks 'completely illegal, null and void' as Beijing extends its gray zone coercion from the South China Sea into the western Pacific. China's Xiang Yang Hong 33 research vessel entered its 26th consecutive day of unauthorized presence near Pag-asa (Thitu) Island, with Beijing's UNCLOS Article 246 diplomatic silence extending to Day 21. The Philippines' three active West Philippine Sea standoffs persist: (1) Xiang Yang Hong 33 near Pag-asa (Day 26, UNCLOS silence Day 21 — longest unanswered Philippine diplomatic instrument under Marcos administration); (2) Scarborough Shoal (PLA STC combat patrols June 1; China CCG law enforcement; 'marine nature reserve' DFA protest still unanswered); (3) Second Thomas Shoal (CCG blockade posture). A new fourth front has opened east of Taiwan in the Pacific, triggered by the Japan-Philippines maritime boundary delimitation talks — marking China's most expansive simultaneous maritime pressure campaign against the Philippine alliance network since the AUKUS announcement in 2021.
